problem: Graph-based ObjectNav methods (ORG, HOZ, TSOG, CGI, AKGVP) inject target relevance only via features or attention and are permutation-invariant with local message passing, so they lack explicit control over information propagation order and struggle with target-dependent importance and long-range dependencies.
motivation: ObjectNav needs an agent to prioritize target-relevant objects and reason over long horizons. Graph-Mamba shows node ordering in a sequence scan lets later nodes aggregate richer context, but it uses generic heuristics such as node degree. The paper asks how to jointly design ordering and edge attributes for ObjectNav, where target relevance gives a natural importance measure.
key_idea: Use LLM-derived commonsense object affinities both to initialize edge embeddings and to sort object nodes by target relevance for a Graph-Mamba scan, with the target placed last, combined with a per-object temporal Mamba scan.
insight: Global ordered scanning is the dominant factor: adding the global scan (GS) raises SR from 66.15 to 78.34, and random ordering drops it to 73.67. Temporal scan adds a further 4.9 SR (78.34 to 83.22), and scanning past-to-current beats current-to-past (83.22 vs 81.24), consistent with the ordering principle. LLM priors are useful but not essential for edges (fixed LLM 77.49 vs learnable random 77.59), while corrupting 30% of the relations lowers SR from 83.22 to 77.92.
method: Object graph construction: a frozen COCO DETR gives per-category features (22x256), boxes and scores, kept as the highest-confidence instance per category; these are concatenated with GloVe 300-d embeddings and a target indicator, and projected to node features (22 nodes).

LLM affinity prior: ChatGPT5 with a chain-of-thought prompt scores co-occurrence and proximity for every object pair in [0,1], giving a 22x22 matrix A; the entries A[i,j] are mapped through a learnable embedding to edge features.
Local branch: GINE edge-aware message passing over observed objects (fully connected among detected categories).

Global target-aware Graph-Mamba: nodes are sorted by h_i = A[i,target] ascending with the target last (+inf), scanned by a causal Mamba, and restored to the original order; the local and global outputs are summed and passed through an FFN, over L_s layers.

Temporal object-track Mamba: a FIFO memory (T=35) of node embeddings is permuted to per-object sequences, and a causal Mamba runs along time (past to current) for each object, with the object order fixed.

Target-conditioned fusion and policy: the target text embedding queries the memory by multi-head cross-attention, an MLP maps the result to 22x7x7, and it is concatenated with the ResNet-18 global feature and the previous action, then a 1x1 conv, a two-layer LSTM (512) and A3C.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 (pretrained) + frozen DETR + GloVe + GINE/Mamba graph encoder + 2-layer LSTM A3C policy (trained end-to-end; ChatGPT5 used offline for the affinity matrix)
setting.training_data: A3C in simulator, several million episodes on AI2-THOR (20 scenes per room type for training) and RoboTHOR (60 training apartments); no extra data besides the LLM-derived affinity matrix
setting.action_space: discrete: MoveAhead, RotateLeft, RotateRight, LookUp, LookDown, Done
setting.privileged: none (LLM commonsense prior over a fixed 22-object vocabulary)

numbers.extra: 22 target categories; mean of 3 test runs; T=35

numbers.eval_set_note: episodes with shortest path length L>=5
episodes with shortest path length L>=5

numbers_note: AI2-THOR and RoboTHOR are not among the canonical names, so they are listed as 'other:'; the paper does not explicitly say 'test' for the reported split and says only 'unseen environments' (test split is 5 scenes per type in AI2-THOR / 10 apartments in RoboTHOR). The RoboTHOR bench string is given without the 'other:' prefix in the entries above to match the canonical RoboTHOR-ObjNav name. Path-length results (L>=10/15/20) are in Table 3 (SR 65.92/42.63/33.40).
results: On AI2-THOR, Graph-MambaNav reaches 83.22 SR / 46.52 SPL (ALL) and 76.09 SR on L>=5, beating the strongest baselines: Memory-MambaNav (81.24 SR, 46.60 SPL) and TSOG (80.04 SR). On RoboTHOR it gets 49.82 SR / 28.67 SPL against CGI+GAIL at 48.30 / 28.77. It also uses 12.58M params and runs at 22.12 FPS versus 62.13M and 11.32 FPS for a Transformer variant.
limitations: Fixed vocabulary of 22 (or 12) object categories with one instance per category; open-vocabulary and multi-instance settings are left to future work.

Depends on the commonsense prior; low-variance relations (e.g. light switch) or layouts that deviate from the prior (pot in RoboTHOR) hurt performance, and 30% noisy relations drops SR by about 5 points.
The real-world evaluation is a single qualitative living-room example with the book target, and SPL gains on RoboTHOR are marginal or slightly below CGI+GAIL.
